'''Charles Brewer-Carías''' (born 10 September 1938 in [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]]) is a Venezuelan [[explorer]] and [[naturalist]]. Known as the "[[Alexander von Humboldt|Humboldt]] of the twentieth century", Brewer-Carías has led more than 200 expeditions to remote parts of the [[Guayana Region, Venezuela|Venezuelan Guayana]], particularly the [[tepui]]s ([[Table (landform)|table mountains]]) of the region. His discoveries include the [[sink hole]]s of [[Cerro Sarisariñama]] and the world's largest known [[quartzite]] cave, [[Cueva Charles Brewer]].<ref name=jstor>[http://plants.jstor.org/person/bm000033570 Brewer Carías, Charles (1938-)]. JSTOR Plant Science.</ref><ref name=CV>{{cite web|url= http://www.plymouth.ac.uk/files/extranet/docs/I_UBC/CVCharlesBrewer.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae: Charles Brewer-Carias. }} University of Plymouth.</ref><ref name=guardian>Carroll, R. (6 April 2010). [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/apr/06/charles-brewer-carias-naturalist-venezuela The British gentleman who became Venezuela's Indiana Jones]. ''The Guardian''.</ref><ref>Aubrecht, R., C. Brewer-Carías, B. Šmída, M. Audy & Ľ. Kováčik (30 January 2008). Anatomy of biologically mediated opal speleothems in the World's largest sandstone cave: Cueva Charles Brewer, Chimantá Plateau, Venezuela. ''Sedimentary Geology'' '''203'''(3–4): 181–195. {{doi|10.1016/j.sedgeo.2007.10.005}}</ref> In 1982, Charles invented a survival knife.

== Recognitions ==
Around 27<ref>Bromfield, T. (December 2010). [http://www.geographical.co.uk/Magazine/People/Charles_Brewer_Carias_-_Dec_10.html Charles Brewer Carias] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111201042906/http://www.geographical.co.uk/Magazine/People/Charles_Brewer_Carias_-_Dec_10.html |date=December 1, 2011 }}. ''Geographical Magazine''.</ref> species of animals and plants have been named in his honour, including the [[bromeliad]] genus ''[[Brewcaria]]''.<ref name="CV" /> 

In 2025, he received the [[Paez Medal of Art]] from the [[Venezuelan American Endowment for the Arts]] in recognition of his extensive work as a Venezuelan naturalist, ethnographer, and explorer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ali |title=The Páez Medal of Art 2025 Charles Brewer-Carías |url=https://vaearts.org/US/the-paez-medal-of-art-2025-charles-brewer-carias/ |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=VAEA |language=en-US}}</ref>
